land.text: Egypt, which Alexander the Great 'conquered' in 332 BC; Ptolemy 'ruled Egypt from 323 BC, nominally in the name of the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV'

predecessors.note: The page's infobox gives 305 BC as the foundation (304 BC by some scholars, who count the kingship); the dossier starts in 323, when Ptolemy took Egypt as satrap and began to rule it, because Cliopatria's own shapes for Egypt run from 307 and the Diadochi settlements are to be drawn from 323.

land.text: Egypt: 'The city passed, with the rest of Egypt, into Roman hands in 30 BC'

successors.note: Octavian seized Egypt in August 30 BC (roman-republic /ledger/214); that dossier runs to 27 BC, after which the province belongs to the Roman Empire. Cleopatra's other lands (Cyprus, 31; Cilicia Aspera, 30; Cyrenaica and central Syria) also passed to Rome; see the ledger.

capitals.name: Alexandria
capitals.note: Infobox and text: 'Alexandria, a Greek polis (city-state) founded by Alexander the Great, became the capital city'. The page names no other seat.

rulers.name: Ptolemy I Soter
rulers.title: satrap of Egypt from 323, king from 305
rulers.note: The Ptolemaic dynasty page prints the reign as 305-282; the entry starts in 323, when Ptolemy took Egypt as satrap (Ptolemaic Kingdom page).

rulers.name: Ptolemy VI Philometor
rulers.note: With Cleopatra II (170-116) and Ptolemy VIII (listed 170-163) as co-rulers; the page prints Ptolemy VI's reigns as 181-164 and 163-145.

rulers.name: Ptolemy VI Philometor
rulers.note: Second reign; brief co-rule with Ptolemy Eupator, 152.

rulers.name: Ptolemy VIII Physcon
rulers.note: The page also lists 170-163 (co-ruler, then king of Cyrene) and 127-116 (after his expulsion from Alexandria by Cleopatra II; reconciled 124). Cleopatra III co-ruler 141-131 and 127-101.

rulers.name: Ptolemy X Alexander I
rulers.note: Cleopatra III co-ruler to 101; Berenice III 101-88.

rulers.name: Ptolemy XI Alexander II
rulers.note: Ruled 19 days alone after murdering Berenice III.

rulers.name: Cleopatra VII Thea Philopator
rulers.note: Co-rulers Ptolemy XIII 51-47, Ptolemy XIV 47-44, Ptolemy XV Caesarion 44-30; Arsinoe IV rival queen 48-47.

correction.text: Not a Ptolemaic shape: Egypt, Syria and southern Anatolia held by Alexander the Great after 332 BC belong to the macedonian-empire dossier; the Ptolemaic state does not begin before 323 BC

keyframe_review.note: 4.2 k cells (1.22 M km2) over Egypt, Syria and Anatolia: Alexander's western conquests, not a Ptolemaic state. The page: 'In 332 BC, Alexander the Great, King of Macedon, conquered Egypt' and 'Ptolemy ruled Egypt from 323 BC'. The infobox of the page gives no area figure to compare (it gives 4.9-7.5 million people c. 150 BC).

correction.text: Egypt, the satrapy given to Ptolemy at the partition of 323 BC

correction.text: Egypt, Cyrenaica, Cyprus and the satrapy of Syria taken from Laomedon

correction.text: Egypt, Cyrenaica and Cyprus, Syria given up in 315

The Wars of the Diadochi page says instead that Syria and Phoenicia were 'under Ptolemy's control' when Antigonus invaded in 314 and that Ptolemy 'controlled Egypt, Syria, Cyrene and Cyprus' after the 311 settlement; Cliopatria draws no Syria in 307-302, which agrees with the Ptolemy I page.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 307 shape without Cyprus (lost to Demetrius after Salamis in 306) and with Cyrenaica, still Ptolemaic until the revolt of about 305

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape without Cyprus (lost after Salamis in 306) and without Cyrenaica (in revolt from 305), for 305-302; for 306 itself Cyrenaica is added (keyframe 306)

Cyprus was lost in 306: 'Demetrius defeated him decisively in a naval battle of Salamis'. Cyrenaica revolted about 305 ('Shortly after Ptolemy declared himself king (c.305 BC), the Cyrenaeans rebelled', Magas of Cyrene page) and was 'finally subjugated in about 300'; so the Cliopatria shape, which has no Cyrenaica, is right for 305-302 once Cyprus is taken out. [Repair pass: the earlier correction added Cyrenaica to 306-302.] No area on the page to compare.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 301 only; Cyrenaica is added from 300 (keyframe 300) and Cyprus from 295 (keyframe 295)

keyframe_review.note: 703 k km2 with Coele-Syria added: 'In 302 he invaded Syria a third time' and after Ipsus 'his fourth occupation of Syria' (Ptolemy I page). The shape has no Cyrenaica, right for 301 while the revolt lasts. The Wars of the Diadochi page says Cilicia and Lycia went to Pleistarchus at Ipsus and that Ptolemy 'recovered Cyprus, eastern Cilicia, and Lycia' about 294, so the Anatolian cells of this shape (Cilicia 97 cells) may be six years early.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 301 shape with Cyrenaica, regained about 300 under Magas

correction.text: Egypt, Coele-Syria, Cyrenaica and, again, Cyprus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'he retook Cyprus in 295 BC' (Ptolemaic Kingdom page; the Ptolemy I page says 295/294). Cliopatria adds Cyprus in 291.
849 k km2: Egypt, Cyrenaica, Cyprus, Coele-Syria and the Anatolian south coast; agrees with the dated gains of Ptolemy I (Cyrenaica about 300, Cyprus 295). No area on the page to compare.
Same outline as 291 (849 k km2); Ptolemy II succeeds in 283 ('who succeeded his father as pharaoh of Egypt in 283 BC') without a territorial change.

944 k km2, 95 k km2 more than 279 (the difference, on the gazetteer, is 345 cells between 19.5-28.2 E and 38.5-42.4 N: Macedon, Thessaly and Thrace). Ptolemy Keraunos 'was displaced in favour of his younger brother Ptolemy II', 'formally relinquished his claim to the Egyptian throne', had himself acclaimed king at Lysimachia after the murder of Seleucus (September 281) and 'ruled for seventeen months before his death in battle against the Gauls in early 279 BC' (Ptolemy Keraunos page); kingdom-of-lysimachus /ledger/23 gives Macedon, Thessaly and Thrace to him. The Ptolemaic Kingdom page's 'fresh conquests as far north as Thrace' is undated and does not support a mainland holding; the earlier ledger events (a 281 gain from Lysimachus, a 279 loss to nobody) are deleted. Keraunos's Macedon needs a dossier (counterparts list).

correction.text: Not a Ptolemaic shape for 281-280: the Cliopatria shape of 283-282 (Egypt, Cyrenaica, Cyprus, Coele-Syria and the Anatolian coasts) is the one to use; the 87 k km2 north of the Aegean (Macedon and Thrace) was Ptolemy Keraunos's

keyframe_review.note: Back to the 291 outline (846 k km2) after the 281-280 shape, which was Ptolemy Keraunos's Macedon and not Ptolemaic (see the 281 verdict); nothing is lost here.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape plus the coastal districts of Caria, Lycia, Pamphylia and Cilicia won in the First Syrian War, from 271

keyframe_review.note: 741 k km2 without Cyrenaica (Magas, 274-250). The shape lacks the First Syrian War gains: 'controlling the Aegean islands (the Nesiotic League) and the coastal districts of Cilicia, Pamphylia, Lycia and Caria' (274-271); Cliopatria shows them only from 264. Use the 264 outline's Anatolian coast from 271.

754 k km2 with the First Syrian War gains (Caria, Lycia, Pamphylia, Cilicia, a few cells of Ionia): 'Ptolemy reconquered these territories by 271 BC'. The shape begins seven years after the dated gain (see the 272 verdict).
678 k km2: Cilicia, Ionia and part of Caria lost in the Second Syrian War (260-253), 'concluded around 253 BC'; the ledger puts the loss in 253, three years after Cliopatria's boundary.

783 k km2 with Cyrenaica back. The Magas page gives no year for the reunion ('Berenice later returned to Egypt to marry Ptolemy III'); the ledger records 247 at confidence 1. [Repair pass: Berenice II's marriage and the return of Cyrenaica are dated 246 (Berenice II page), so Cliopatria's shape is one year early for 247.] Review fix fx-33 (2026-11-01): the years are now 246-240. Berenice II page reread: "Berenice married Ptolemy III in 246 BCE after his accession to the throne", which brought "Cyrenaica back into the Ptolemaic realm"; the page does not mention 247. The cyrenaica dossier still holds the land in 247 (its keyframe _-272 runs to 247), so a shape from 247 took its cells a year early.

correction.text: shape unchanged; the years are 246-240, one year later than Cliopatria's 247 (Cyrenaica returns with Berenice II's marriage in 246)

keyframe_review.note: 799 k km2: the northern Syrian coast (Seleucia Pieria, modern Hatay) and more of Cilicia added: 'In exchange for peace in 241 BC, Ptolemy was awarded new territories on the northern coast of Syria'. The shape begins two years after the dated gain. Page gives no area; the Ptolemaic page calls the Third Syrian War the 'zenith of the Ptolemaic power'.

739 k km2 without Coele-Syria, Phoenicia and Seleucia Pieria: 219 BC, Antiochus 'recaptured Seleucia Pieria as well as cities in Phoenicia, amongst them Tyre'. Right for 218-217; the zone is contested in the ledger until Raphia.

778 k km2 with Coele-Syria again: Raphia in 217, 'Ptolemy's victory preserved his control over Coele-Syria'. The page does not say whether the Phoenician cities came back; the shape shows them Ptolemaic.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 212-206 only

keyframe_review.note: 779 k km2 with the whole of Upper Egypt, but the Thebaid was in revolt from 205: 'In the autumn of 205 BC, the leader of the revolt was crowned pharaoh in Thebes as Haronnophris'. Right only for 212-206; see keyframe 205. The bbox reaches 7.1 E on a few cells, an artefact.

correction.text: The 203 shape without the Thebaid held by the rebel pharaohs (all Upper Egypt but Ptolemais and Aswan) and without Lower Nubia, taken by Kush about 204

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the Thebaid lost: 'Haronnophris then ruled over a territory comprising more or less all of Upper Egypt', except Ptolemais and Aswan, from Abydos to Per-Hathor; 'The troops of Ptolemy V captured Thebes in December 199 BC'. Cliopatria's Ankhwennefer shape is the nearest outline of the rebel land. Lower Nubia (13 cells of the shape, south of Aswan) is dropped: Kush took it about 204 (Kingdom of Kush page; Great Theban Revolt page: 'all Ptolemaic territories south of Aswan, including the island of Philae').

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape without Lower Nubia (Kush's since about 204), for 199-198 only

keyframe_review.note: 780 k km2, Coele-Syria and the Anatolian coast still Ptolemaic; right for 199-198, after Thebes was retaken (December 199). The rebel pharaoh held the Thebaid in 205-200 (keyframe 205). Antiochus III takes Coele-Syria by 198 ('completed the subjugation of Coele-Syria in 198 BC'). Lower Nubia (13 cells) is dropped for the years Kush held it, 204-186.

506 k km2: Coele-Syria and the Anatolian coast gone (Antiochus III, 198: 'went on to raid Ptolemy's remaining coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia'), and the Thebaid out again: 'Chaonnophris regained control of the Thebaid around 197 BC'. Thebes was retaken in 191; the shape's partial Upper Egypt stands as the Cliopatria compromise.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 188-186 only

keyframe_review.note: 570 k km2 still without most of Upper Egypt, but the revolt ended earlier than Cliopatria's Ankhwennefer row (to 171): 'The rebel pharaoh Chaonnophris and his army were defeated' on 27 August 186 BC by the army under Komanos. Right for 188-186; see keyframe 185.

correction.text: Egypt, Cyrenaica and Cyprus, the Thebaid recovered after August 186

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Upper Egypt whole again after 186. The kingdom's 164 shape (Egypt, Cyrenaica, Cyprus) is the outline to use.

correction.text: The kingdom as before and after (Egypt, Cyrenaica, Cyprus); the Seleucid occupation of 170-168 is hatched via the occupation events

keyframe_review.note: 156 k km2 (Cyprus, Cyrenaica and a corner of the delta), i.e. Cliopatria hands the Nile valley to the Seleucid row for 170-165. The page: Antiochus IV 'took Pelusium, Memphis, and Cyprus' but 'withdrew after the Roman ultimatum' of 168; Ptolemy VI and VIII went on reigning. Draw the kingdom whole and the Seleucid presence as occupation (ledger).

correction.text: Egypt and Cyprus without Cyrene, which Ptolemy VIII held as a separate kingdom from 163 to 145

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cyrenaica separate. 'As a result of Roman intervention, Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene' in 163 after Alexandria recalled Ptolemy VI; Cyprus stayed with Ptolemy VI. In 145 'The Ptolemaic empire was now limited to Egypt, Cyprus, and Cyrene'. (The Ptolemy Apion page lists Ptolemy VIII as king of Cyrene and Cyprus, 163-116, which this page contradicts for Cyprus.)

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 164 and 145-127

keyframe_review.note: 680 k km2, the full kingdom. Right for 164 and for 145-127, after Ptolemy VIII 'return[ed] from Cyrene' and became king in 145; wrong for 163-146 (keyframe 163). No area on the Ptolemaic page. Review fx-33 (2026-11-01): given from -164 to -164; without years it ran on Cliopatria's -164..-127 and, alive beside keyframe _-163 (-163..-146), put Cyrene back into the -163 keyframe. From -145 the ledger gain (ledger 62) restores Cyrene and no keyframe is needed until _-126.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 126-106 only

keyframe_review.note: 669 k km2. Includes Cyrenaica until Ptolemy Apion's separate kingdom: 'apparently given Cyrene as a separate kingdom ca. 105-101 BC'. Right for 126-106. The civil war 132-127 (Cleopatra II held Alexandria) ends just before this shape starts.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 105 to 59 and 47 to 37; Cyprus is out for 58-48 (keyframe 58) and Cilicia Aspera is in for 36-35 (keyframe 36)

keyframe_review.note: 566 k km2, Egypt and Cyprus without Cyrenaica: right from about 105 (Apion), five years after Cliopatria's boundary; 'Ptolemy died in 96 BC without heirs' and left Cyrenaica to Rome. The Ptolemy VIII page gives Ptolemy X as 'King of Cyprus from 114 to 107 BC', a separate Cypriot kingdom the shape does not show. [Repair pass: Cliopatria keeps Cyprus continuously to 32, but Rome annexed it in 58 and Caesar returned it in 47 (Roman Cyprus page), so the shape is narrowed to the years Cyprus was Ptolemaic.]

correction.text: Egypt without Cyprus, which Rome annexed in 58 and Caesar returned in 47

correction.text: Egypt and Cyprus with Cilicia Aspera, given by Antony in 36

correction.text: Egypt, Cyprus, Cyrenaica (Libya), central Syria and Cilicia Aspera under Cleopatra VII after the Donations of Alexandria

Cliopatria's 31 shape is not this. [Repair pass: Cilicia Aspera (36 grant) added; the keyframe now ends in 32 because Cyprus returns to Rome in 31.]

correction.text: Egypt, Cyrenaica, central Syria and Cilicia Aspera as in keyframe 34, without Cyprus (back to Rome after Actium in 31); not Antony's eastern provinces

keyframe_review.note: 1.27 M km2 over Anatolia, Greece and Syria (4.3 k cells): Antony's whole eastern command, not Cleopatra's kingdom. The Donations page gives her Egypt, Cyprus, Libya and central Syria; the Ptolemaic page gives no year for Actium ('Their naval forces met at Actium').

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape, unchanged, for 30 BC only; 29-28 belongs to Rome

keyframe_review.note: 554 k km2, Egypt alone. Right for 30 BC only: 'Cleopatra and her handmaidens committed suicide on 12 August 30 BC' and 'The city passed, with the rest of Egypt, into Roman hands in 30 BC'. The shape of 29-28 is Roman Egypt, for the roman-empire dossier.

ledger.note: 323: Ptolemy takes Egypt as satrap. 'Ptolemy ruled Egypt from 323 BC, nominally in the name of the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV'; Alexander 'conquered Egypt' in 332. The infobox dates the kingdom from 305 (see the identity note).

region.text: Egypt, Ptolemy's satrapy, ruled 'nominally in the name of the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV'

ledger.note: 323: Ptolemy holds Egypt as satrap of the joint kings. 'Ptolemy ruled Egypt from 323 BC, nominally in the name of the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV' (Ptolemaic Kingdom page). Mirrors macedonian-empire /ledger/43 (June 323, Partition of Babylon); here the kingdom is the vassal and the empire the counterpart. The vassal_end is the 321 event below.

322: Ptolemy's general Ophellas takes Cyrenaica. Ophellas was 'sent, in 322 BC, at the head of a considerable army'; 'Ptolemaic control over Cyrene itself and its dependencies was established and Ophellas remained as its governor' 'from around 322 BC until his death in 308 BC' (Ophellas page). The Ptolemy I Soter page: 'Ptolemy quickly moved, without authorization, to subjugate Cyrenaica' (undated); a revolt in Cyrene was crushed in 313 and the country was 'finally subjugated in about 300 and placed under his stepson Magas'. Cliopatria keeps a separate Cyrenaica row to 292. The year is the page's for the sending; the completion is undated.

region.text: Egypt, 'Egypt with Libya' confirmed to Ptolemy at Triparadisus

ledger.note: 321: Ptolemy's Egypt leaves the empire's tint. 'The Partition of Triparadisus was a power-sharing agreement passed at Triparadisus in 321 BC'; Antipater regent; Ptolemy received 'Egypt with Libya, and all the vast waste beyond it' (Partition of Triparadisus page). The page does not call him independent: 321 is the year macedonian-empire /ledger/46 ends the vassalage (confidence 2 there too), agreed with eu-02. The alternatives are 310/309 (Alexander IV's death) and 305 (the royal title, Ptolemaic Kingdom page). macedonian-empire /ledger/49 reads the same moment as a loss of 'Egypt and Libya'; here Cyrenaica is the 322 gain from the Cyrenaicans, so no separate gain is recorded.

region.text: Laomedon's satrapy of Syria, with Phoenicia, Coele-Syria and Judea

ledger.note: 318: Ptolemy occupies Syria and takes Laomedon. 'His first occupation of Syria was in 318.' The Laomedon article: Ptolemy offered to buy the government, then sent Nicanor, who captured Laomedon ('unable to offer any effective resistance') and sent him to Egypt.

region.text: 'a protectorate over the petty kings of Cyprus'

ledger.note: 318: Ptolemy places the Cypriot kings under his protection. 'His first occupation of Syria was in 318, and he established at the same time a protectorate over the petty kings of Cyprus' (Ptolemy I Soter page). Replaces the earlier gain 'neither page dates' (confidence 1). The vassal is the city-kings as the page names them, not a state with a dossier; the protectorate ends with the 313 reconquest.

region.text: Syria and Phoenicia, evacuated on the outbreak of the war with Antigonus

ledger.note: 315: Ptolemy gives up Syria. Antigonus's expansion led Ptolemy, 'on the outbreak of war, [to] evacuate Syria'. The Wars of the Diadochi page has Antigonus invading Syria and Phoenicia 'under Ptolemy's control' in 314. [Repair pass: counterpart changed from antigonid-dynasty (which begins in 306) to macedonian-empire, whose dossier holds Antigonus's Syria until its 306 split (macedonian-empire /ledger/63); eu-02 is asked for the matching 315 gain of Syria.]
313: revolt in Cyrene. 'A revolt in Cyrene was crushed' the same year (313).
313: the Cyrene revolt is crushed.

region.text: the Cypriot kings, whose island Ptolemy 're-conquered' in 313

ledger.note: 313: the protectorate over the Cypriot kings gives way to direct rule. 'In Cyprus, he fought the partisans of Antigonus, and re-conquered the island (313)' (Ptolemy I Soter page); that the protectorate ends here is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Cyprus, 're-conquered' from the partisans of Antigonus

ledger.note: 313: Ptolemy reconquers Cyprus. 'In Cyprus, he fought the partisans of Antigonus, and re-conquered the island (313)' (Ptolemy I Soter page). Counterpart macedonian-empire stands for Antigonus's side, which that dossier holds until 306; the island passes 'entirely to the Antigonids' in 306 (event below).

region.text: Coele-Syria and Palestine, fought over at Gaza

ledger.note: 312: Ptolemy fights for Syria. 'At Gaza he defeated Demetrius, who commanded a smaller force including 43 elephants' (the Wars of the Diadochi page: 'Ptolemy and Seleucus invaded from Egypt and defeated Demetrius in the Battle of Gaza'). The Gaza year is given by the article's link title. [Repair pass: counterpart changed from antigonid-dynasty (which begins in 306) to macedonian-empire, whose dossier holds Antigonus's Syria until its 306 split (macedonian-empire /ledger/63); eu-02 is asked for the matching 315 gain of Syria.]

311: peace. 'In 311, a peace was concluded between the combatants.' The Wars of the Diadochi page then has Ptolemy in control of 'Egypt, Syria, Cyrene and Cyprus'; the Ptolemy I page and Cliopatria show no Syria for Ptolemy until 302-301. [Repair pass: counterpart changed from antigonid-dynasty (which begins in 306) to macedonian-empire, whose dossier holds Antigonus's Syria until its 306 split (macedonian-empire /ledger/63); eu-02 is asked for the matching 315 gain of Syria.]
308: Ptolemy takes Corinth. He 'took possession of Corinth, Sicyon and Megara (308 BC)' (the Ptolemaic Kingdom page: 309). From whom the page does not say.

306: Demetrius takes Cyprus. 'Demetrius defeated him decisively in a naval battle of Salamis'; Cyprus passed to the Antigonids (Ptolemaic Kingdom page: 'he lost Cyprus after a naval battle in 306 BC').
305: Ptolemy takes the title of king. 'In 305 BC, Ptolemy took the title of basileus and pharaoh' (304 BC for some scholars, who count by another calendar); the satrapy becomes the Ptolemaic Kingdom.

305: Cyrene rebels against Ptolemy. 'Shortly after Ptolemy declared himself king (c.305 BC), the Cyrenaeans rebelled' (Magas of Cyrene page). Mirrors cyrenaica /ledger/4; the pages have Cyrenaica 'after a series of rebellions' finally subjugated about 300 (Ptolemy I page). The 305 year is the page's 'c.305'.
305: the revolt of Cyrene against Ptolemy opens and is fought over until about 300 (cyrenaica /ledger/5).

304: Demetrius takes the Ptolemaic holdings on the isthmus. 'in 304-303 BC, he successively seized Panactum, Phyle, Kechries, Epidaurus, Sicyon, Corinth, Bura' (Demetrius I of Macedon page; 303 is the end of the page's range, and macedonian-empire /ledger/65 uses 304). The page does not call the garrisons Ptolemaic and does not name Megara; that Corinth and Sicyon were Ptolemy's comes from the Ptolemy I page (308). Replaces the earlier 302 bridge (confidence 1).
302: Ptolemy invades Syria a third time. 'In 302 he invaded Syria a third time' (Ptolemaic Kingdom page: he 'secure[d] Coele-Syria and Palestine as well as parts of Anatolia').

301: Ptolemy holds Coele-Syria after Ipsus. Antigonus was 'defeated and slain by Lysimachus and Seleucus at the Battle of Ipsus in 301', which led to Ptolemy's 'fourth occupation of Syria'. Seleucus's claim to the land, awarded to him in the division (Wars of the Diadochi page), is the root of the Syrian Wars.
301: the fighting for Coele-Syria ends at Ipsus.
300: the revolt ends. 'Around 300 BC, Ptolemy dispatched Magas, then about 20 years old, to reconquer Cyrene' (Magas of Cyrene page).

region.text: Cyrenaica, reconquered and placed under Magas

ledger.note: 300: Magas reconquers Cyrene for Ptolemy. 'Around 300 BC, Ptolemy dispatched Magas ... to reconquer Cyrene'; 'Magas subsequently served as the province's governor' (Magas of Cyrene page). The Ptolemy I Soter page: 'Cyrenaica, after a series of rebellions, was finally subjugated in about 300 and placed under his stepson Magas'. Mirrors cyrenaica /ledger/7.

295: Ptolemy retakes Cyprus. 'he retook Cyprus in 295 BC' (the Ptolemy I page: 'reconquered Cyprus in 295/294'). The Wars of the Diadochi page has him recover 'Cyprus, eastern Cilicia, and Lycia' in the context of 294.

274: Ptolemy II annexes Lower Nubia. 'In 275 or 274 BC, Ptolemy II (r. 283-246 BC) sent an army to Nubia, and defeated the Kingdom of Kush, annexing to Egypt the area later known as Triakontaschoinos' (Kingdom of Kush page; the Dodecaschoenus page has the same sentence); 274 matches the kingdom-of-kush dossier. The Ptolemaic Kingdom page: 'In the 270s BC, Ptolemy II defeated the Kingdom of Kush in war'. Lower Nubia for the page's Triakontaschoinos is the researcher's reading. Replaces the earlier 275 bridge (confidence 1).

274: Cyrenaica breaks away under Magas. Magas 'tried to wrest independence' after Ptolemy I's death and 'crowned himself King'; the page disputes the date (283-280 or 276/274; infobox reign from 276). He died in 250.

region.text: Caria and most of Cilicia, where the war's gains lay

ledger.note: 274: the First Syrian War begins ('First Syrian War (274-271 BC)').
271: the First Syrian War ends in a Ptolemaic victory.

region.text: the coastal districts of Cilicia, Pamphylia, Lycia and Caria, and the Aegean islands

ledger.note: 271: Ptolemy II wins the Anatolian coast. By the end of the First Syrian War (274-271) he was 'controlling the Aegean islands (the Nesiotic League) and the coastal districts of Cilicia, Pamphylia, Lycia and Caria in Asia Minor'; the Syrian Wars page: 'Ptolemy reconquered these territories by 271 BC'.

region.text: the Anatolian coast Ptolemy lost: parts of Cilicia, Ionia and Caria

ledger.note: 260: the Second Syrian War begins ('Second Syrian War (260-253 BC)'); 'Antigonus' fleet defeated Ptolemy's at the Battle of Cos in 261 BC'.
253: the Second Syrian War ends, 'concluded around 253 BC with the marriage of Antiochus to Ptolemy's daughter'.

region.text: parts of Cilicia, Pamphylia, Ionia and Caria

ledger.note: 253: Ptolemy loses ground in Anatolia. Ptolemy 'lost ground in Cilicia, Pamphylia, and Ionia, while Antiochus II regained Miletus and Ephesus'; the Ptolemaic page: 'some of these territories were lost near the end of his reign as a result of the Second Syrian War'. The year is the peace; Cliopatria's boundary is 256.

region.text: Cyrenaica, brought back by the marriage of Berenice II to Ptolemy III

ledger.note: 246: Cyrenaica returns to Egypt with Berenice II's marriage. 'Berenice married Ptolemy III in 246 BCE after his accession to the throne'; 'This marriage led to the re-incorporation of Cyrenaica into the Ptolemaic empire' (Berenice II page). Matches the cyrenaica dossier (-246). Cliopatria's Ptolemaic shape with Cyrenaica starts in 247, one year early. Replaces the earlier 247 bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: the northern Syrian coast and Cilicia taken in the war

ledger.note: 246: the Third Syrian War begins: 'Ptolemy declared war on Laodice's newly crowned son, Seleucus II, in 246 BC'; Ptolemy III 'briefly occupied Antioch' and reached Babylon.

246: the Cyclades pass to Antigonus Gonatas. 'These victories were marred by the loss of the Cyclades to Antigonus Gonatas in the Battle of Andros' (Syrian Wars page, no year); the Battle of Andros page lists the battle as '246 BC' between Ptolemaic Egypt and Antigonid Macedonia and says nothing of the result. Cliopatria's Ptolemaic shapes hold only two Cyclades cells, so this is a ledger-only record. antigonid-dynasty has no matching gain yet (asked of eu-02).

region.text: the northern Syrian coast and Cilicia

ledger.note: 241: peace ends the Third Syrian War.

region.text: new territories on the northern coast of Syria, with Seleucia Pieria

ledger.note: 241: Ptolemy III at his height. 'In exchange for peace in 241 BC, Ptolemy was awarded new territories on the northern coast of Syria' (Seleucia Pieria, the port of Antioch). The Cilician cells are the shape's, not the page's. The Cyclades went to Antigonus Gonatas at Andros.

region.text: Phoenicia and Coele-Syria, where Antiochus III advanced

ledger.note: 219: the Fourth Syrian War begins ('Fourth Syrian War (219-217 BC)'); Antiochus 'recaptured Seleucia Pieria as well as cities in Phoenicia, amongst them Tyre'.

region.text: Seleucia Pieria and the cities of Phoenicia, among them Tyre

ledger.note: 219: Antiochus III retakes Seleucia Pieria, the port of Antioch, and Phoenician cities including Tyre.

217: Raphia. 'In the summer of 217 BC, Ptolemy engaged and defeated the long-delayed Antiochus'; 'Ptolemy's victory preserved his control over Coele-Syria, and the weak king declined to advance further'. Seleucia Pieria stayed Seleucid.

region.text: all of Upper Egypt but Ptolemais and Aswan

ledger.note: 205: Upper Egypt secedes. 'In the autumn of 205 BC, the leader of the revolt was crowned pharaoh in Thebes as Haronnophris', who 'ruled over a territory comprising more or less all of Upper Egypt' except the Greek strongholds of Ptolemais and Aswan, from Abydos to Per-Hathor. The Ptolemaic page calls him Horwennefer.

region.text: Lower Nubia, south of Aswan, including Philae

ledger.note: 204: Kush takes Lower Nubia during the Theban revolt. 'there was a serious revolt at the end of the reign of Ptolemy IV, around 204 BC' and 'the Kushites reasserted their control' (Kingdom of Kush page); the Great Theban Revolt page, undated: Meroe 'took advantage of the situation to invade Egypt and Lower Nubia from the south' and 'take control of all Ptolemaic territories south of Aswan, including the island of Philae'; the Dodecaschoenus page: 'Ptolemaic control over Lower Nubia collapsed c. 205 BC'. Mirrors kingdom-of-kush /ledger/14 (-204). The 204 date is the Kush page's; the Revolt page gives none.

region.text: Coele-Syria and the coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia

ledger.note: 202: the Fifth Syrian War begins ('202/201-195 BC' in the page's table; the text dates no first campaign). Panium, 200: 'the battle of Panium in 200 BC transferred Coele-Syria from Ptolemaic to Seleucid control' (Ptolemaic Kingdom page).

region.text: Miletus, Samos and footholds in Caria

ledger.note: 201: Philip V seizes Ptolemaic Samos, Miletus and Carian footholds. Philip moved 'to capture Egyptian-held territory from the boy king Ptolemy V', 'besieging Samos and capturing Miletus', then 'invaded Caria'; the navies of Rhodes and Pergamon 'clashed with Philip's off Chios and Lade (near Miletus) in 201 BC' (Philip V of Macedon page; it says 'Egyptian-held' rather than Ptolemaic). Mirrors antigonid-dynasty /ledger/52 (-201).
199: Ptolemaic troops retake the Thebaid. 'The troops of Ptolemy V captured Thebes in December 199 BC' and the first rebel pharaoh died that year.

198: Coele-Syria is lost. 'Antiochus completed the subjugation of Coele-Syria in 198 BC and went on to raid Ptolemy's remaining coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia'; a treaty of 195 confirmed it and Ptolemy V married Cleopatra I.

region.text: the remaining coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia, with Lycia, Pamphylia and the islands

ledger.note: 198: the Anatolian coast is lost. The page speaks of raids on 'Ptolemy's remaining coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia'; Cliopatria drops all the Anatolian cells and the Aegean islands in 197.
198: the fighting for Coele-Syria ends; the treaty of 195 only confirms it.
197: the Thebaid is lost again. 'Chaonnophris regained control of the Thebaid around 197 BC' (the Ptolemaic page calls him Ankhwennefer, son of Horwennefer).
195: the fighting at Asyut begins; 'heavy fighting from 195 to 191 BC' as Chaonnophris's territory expanded north toward Asyut.
191: the fighting at Asyut ends.
191: the army under Ptolemaios retakes Thebes ('retook control of Thebes the same year').

186: the revolt of the south is over. Chaonnophris was 'defeated on August 27, 186 BC, by the Ptolemaic army under Komanos', captured and later executed at Memphis; the Ptolemaic page: 'The revolutionary dynasty was finally defeated in 186 BC'.

region.text: Lower Nubia, 'Ptolemaic rule was re-established over Upper Egypt and Lower Nubia'

ledger.note: 186: the Ptolemies re-establish rule over Lower Nubia. 'in August 186 BC, the Ptolemaic army defeated the forces of Hugronaphor's successor Chaonnophris. Ptolemaic rule was re-established over Upper Egypt and Lower Nubia' (Dodecaschoenus page); in 157 BC Ptolemy VI 'renewed the donation of the incomes of the entire Dodekaschoinos to the Temple of Isis'. The Ptolemaic Kingdom page says only that 'Throughout the 160s and 150s BC, Ptolemy VI also reasserted Ptolemaic control over the northern part of Nubia', and the Kingdom of Kush page gives no year: the pages disagree, and 186 is the only page that dates it. kingdom-of-kush has no matching loss yet. Replaces the earlier 155 bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Egypt outside Alexandria, with Pelusium and Memphis, and Cyprus

ledger.note: 170: Antiochus IV invades Egypt. 'He reached the strategically important town of Pelusium in November 170 BC'; the Ptolemaic page: Antiochus IV 'invaded Egypt and captured Philometor'. He took 'Pelusium, Memphis, and Cyprus'; Alexandria was not taken. The page notes revolts in Egypt in 168-164.

region.text: Egypt and Cyprus, evacuated on the Roman ultimatum

ledger.note: 168: the Seleucid forces leave. Antiochus's control collapsed and he 'invaded again in 168 BC'; Popillius ordered him to evacuate Egypt and Cyprus (the Day of Eleusis, not dated explicitly by the page, within the 168 campaign).

region.text: Cyrene, awarded to Ptolemy VIII: the Cyrenaica cells of the kingdom's 164 shape (the same 343 cells as cyrenaica ledger 11)

ledger.note: 163: Cyrene goes to Ptolemy VIII. He 'was expelled in turn in 163 BC' from Alexandria; 'As a result of Roman intervention, Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene'. Cyprus stays with his brother Ptolemy VI. [Review fx-33 (2026-11-01): region narrowed from the whole gazetteer Cyrenaica region (2,496 cells, mostly desert outside the kingdom's shape) to its 343 cells inside Cliopatria's 164 shape, matching the cyrenaica mirror; Ptolemy VIII page: 'Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene' (163), 'the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene' (145).]
161: Ptolemy VIII invades Cyprus. 'He launched a military expedition to Cyprus in 161 BC' (promised to him by the Romans); Cypriot resistance forced him to abandon it after up to a year.
160: the Cyprus expedition is abandoned.
154: Ptolemy VI besieges his brother. 'Ptolemy VIII was besieged by his older brother at Lapethus and was captured'; he agreed to leave Cyprus in exchange for keeping Cyrenaica.
154: Ptolemy VIII gives up Cyprus.

region.text: Cyrene: the Cyrenaica cells of the kingdom's 164 shape (the same 343 cells as cyrenaica ledger 12)

ledger.note: 145: Ptolemy VIII reunites the kingdom. After Ptolemy VI died on campaign 'the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene, assume the kingship'; 'The Ptolemaic empire was now limited to Egypt, Cyprus, and Cyrene.' [Review fx-33 (2026-11-01): region narrowed from the whole gazetteer Cyrenaica region (2,496 cells, mostly desert outside the kingdom's shape) to its 343 cells inside Cliopatria's 164 shape, matching the cyrenaica mirror; Ptolemy VIII page: 'Ptolemy VIII was awarded control of Cyrene' (163), 'the Alexandrians called on Ptolemy VIII to return from Cyrene' (145).]
132: civil war in Egypt, 'from 132/1 to 127/6 BC, in which Cleopatra II controlled Alexandria'.
127: 'Cleopatra II took her treasury and fled Alexandria for the court of Demetrius II. In her absence, Ptolemy VIII finally reconquered Alexandria.'

region.text: Cyrenaica, a separate kingdom of Ptolemy Apion

ledger.note: 105: Cyrene becomes a separate kingdom. 'Ptolemy Apion was apparently given Cyrene as a separate kingdom ca. 105-101 BC'; 'Ptolemy died in 96 BC without heirs' and left Cyrenaica to Rome. Ptolemy VIII's page lists Apion as king of Cyrenaica 'from an uncertain date'. Cliopatria shows the break in 110.

58: Rome annexes Cyprus. 'The lex Clodia de Cypro was passed by the plebeian council in 58 BC'; Cato the Younger was sent to annex the island, 'Cato was proconsul of Cyprus from 58-56 BC', and Ptolemy of Cyprus killed himself (Roman Cyprus page). Mirrors roman-republic /ledger/173.

47: Caesar returns Cyprus to the Ptolemies. 'Julius Caesar agreed to return control of Cyprus to the Ptolemaic Kingdom'; timeline '47 BC - Cyprus was restored under the Egyptian rule of Cleopatra' (Roman Cyprus page, no month). Mirrors roman-republic /ledger/183.

36: Antony gives Cilicia Aspera to Cleopatra. 'Further changes were made by Marcus Antonius in 36 BC, when he gave Cyprus and Cilicia Aspera to Cleopatra VII' (Cilicia (Roman province) page; Cyprus was already hers since 47). The Donations of Alexandria page: 'a similar donation ceremony had taken place two years earlier at Antioch in 36 BC' (lands not listed). Mirrors roman-republic /ledger/200; the circle is the one that dossier uses (no gazetteer name for Cilicia Aspera).

region.text: Libya (Cyrenaica) and central Syria, confirmed to Cleopatra

ledger.note: 34: the Donations of Alexandria. In the autumn of 34 'Antony confirmed Cleopatra as queen of Egypt, Cyprus, Libya and central Syria'; Cleopatra Selene 'got Cyrenaica and Libya'. Cyprus was already in Cliopatria's Ptolemaic shape since 110.

31: Cyprus returns to Rome after Actium. '31 BC - Battle of Actium, Marc Antony and Cleopatra were defeated by Augustus and Cyprus returns to Roman rule' (Roman Cyprus page, year only). Mirrors roman-republic /ledger/211.

30: Cleopatra's Cilicia Aspera passes to Rome. The Cilicia (Roman province) page gives only the grant in 36 and that 'Augustus placed this territory under the rule of king Archelaus of Cappadocia in 25 BC'; 30 is the bridge, as in roman-republic /ledger/213 (confidence 1).

30: Egypt passes to Rome. 'The city passed, with the rest of Egypt, into Roman hands in 30 BC'; 'Cleopatra and her handmaidens committed suicide on 12 August 30 BC'. [Reviewer me-05-b: counterpart set to roman-republic, whose dossier runs to 27 BC and records the August 30 BC gain of Egypt from this kingdom.]

region.text: Cleopatra's Egypt, Libya and central Syria (Cyprus and Cilicia Aspera were already lost)

ledger.note: 30: the Ptolemaic Kingdom ends with the death of Cleopatra VII (12 August); Egypt, with Cyrenaica and central Syria, goes to Rome. Cyprus (31) and Cilicia Aspera (30) have their own loss events. Counterpart roman-republic, whose dossier runs to 27 BC and records the August 30 BC gain of Egypt from this kingdom; Cliopatria carries the last shape to 28.

wars.name: Wars of the Diadochi
wars.outcome: Ptolemy keeps Egypt and Cyrenaica, loses Cyprus (306) and wins Coele-Syria at Ipsus (301). Ptolemy defeats Demetrius at Gaza (312); a peace is made in 311; Seleucus and Lysimachus kill Antigonus at Ipsus.
wars.note: The page's infobox gives the First War as 321-319 and the Second as 318-316, the Third as 315-311; it has little on Ptolemy. Dates for Ptolemy come from the Ptolemy I Soter page.

wars.name: Magas' war against Ptolemy II
wars.outcome: Cyrenaica independent under Magas until his death in 250; Cyrenaica rejoined Egypt by the marriage of Berenice II to Ptolemy III.
wars.note: 'The date of this is also disputed'; Magas attacked Egypt from the west but had to cancel his operations because of a revolt by the Marmaridae.

wars.name: First Syrian War
wars.outcome: Ptolemaic victory: Ptolemy II reconquered the territories Antiochus I had taken, extending Ptolemaic rule into Caria and most of Cilicia.

wars.name: Second Syrian War
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: Ptolemy lost ground in Cilicia, Pamphylia and Ionia; Antiochus II regained Miletus and Ephesus; peace c. 253 by a dynastic marriage.

wars.name: Third Syrian War

zones.text: the northern Syrian coast and Cilicia

wars.outcome: Ptolemy III's conquests: victories in Syria and Anatolia, Antioch briefly occupied, Babylon reached; the 241 peace gave him the northern Syrian coast (Seleucia Pieria) at the zenith of Ptolemaic power.
wars.note: Lost the Cyclades to Antigonus Gonatas at the battle of Andros ('These victories were marred by the loss of the Cyclades to Antigonus Gonatas in the Battle of Andros', Syrian Wars page, no year); the Battle of Andros page lists it as 246 BC. Recorded as a 246 loss event.

wars.name: Fourth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Raphia (217): Ptolemy IV defeated Antiochus III and kept Coele-Syria; Seleucia Pieria stayed Seleucid.

wars.name: Great Theban Revolt
wars.outcome: The Thebaid broke away under Horwennefer/Haronnophris (205-199) and Ankhwennefer/Chaonnophris (c. 197-186); Thebes retaken December 199 and again 191; Chaonnophris defeated 27 August 186.
wars.note: The Great Theban Revolt page names the rebel pharaohs Haronnophris and Chaonnophris; the Ptolemaic Kingdom page names them Horwennefer and Ankhwennefer.

wars.name: Fifth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Antiochus III took Coele-Syria (subjugation complete 198) and raided the coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia; a treaty of 195 left him Coele-Syria and married Ptolemy V to Cleopatra I.
wars.note: Ran alongside the Second Macedonian War; Rome told Philip and Antiochus in 200 not to invade Egypt.

wars.name: Sixth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Antiochus IV took Pelusium, Memphis and Cyprus but failed to take Alexandria; after the Roman ultimatum at Eleusis he evacuated Egypt and Cyprus; revolts in Egypt 168-164.

wars.name: Ptolemy VI and Ptolemy VIII over Cyprus and Cyrene
wars.outcome: Ptolemy VIII, given Cyrene by Roman decision in 163, invaded Cyprus in 161 and was besieged and captured at Lapethus in 154; he left Cyprus to his brother and kept Cyrenaica.

wars.name: Ptolemaic civil war of 132-127
wars.outcome: Cleopatra II held Alexandria 132/1-127; she fled to the court of Demetrius II and Ptolemy VIII reconquered the city.

wars.name: War of Actium
wars.outcome: Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra; Cleopatra killed herself on 12 August 30 BC and Egypt passed to Rome.
wars.note: The page says only 'Their naval forces met at Actium' and gives no year; the starting year is Cliopatria's last full shape (-31).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given on the pages opened. The Nile valley and delta are firm; the desert margins (Sinai, the Western Desert, Lower Nubia), the Cyrenaican steppe and every overseas holding (Cyprus, Aegean islands, the Anatolian and Syrian coasts) are approximate, and the Coele-Syria frontier shifted in each Syrian War.

notes: Page budget: nine pages for 26 Cliopatria shapes, extended in the repair pass (2026-10-19) by thirteen pages opened for the reviewer's findings. Not settled: (1) Start: the infobox gives 305 BC (304 for some), but the dossier starts in 323, when Ptolemy took Egypt as satrap, ruling 'nominally in the name of the joint kings'; the macedonian-empire dossier holds Egypt as its vassal 323-321 and the ledger now mirrors that (vassal_start 323, vassal_end 321, Triparadisus). Cliopatria draws no Ptolemaic shape for 323-308 and labels Alexander's conquests of 331-324 'Ptolemaic' (both wrong). (2) Cyrenaica: Cliopatria keeps its own Cyrenaica row to 292, 272-248 and 110-92; the ledger follows the cyrenaica dossier: taken 322 (Ophellas), lost to a revolt about 305, regained about 300 under Magas, Magas's kingdom 274 (cyrenaica says 276; the Magas page says 283-280 or 276/274), back in 246 (Berenice II), Ptolemy VIII's separate kingdom 163-145 (no Cliopatria row), Ptolemy Apion about 105. (3) The Thebaid revolt 205-186: Cliopatria's Ankhwennefer row (to 171) runs 15 years past the page's defeat and does not cover Horwennefer's regime of 205-199; counterpart 'ankhwennefer' is used for both. Lower Nubia goes to Kush about 204 (Kingdom of Kush page) and returns in 186 on the Dodecaschoenus page; the Ptolemaic Kingdom page has the reassertion in the 160s-150s and the Kush page gives no year, so the 186 date is the one page that dates it. (4) Counterpart 'antigonid-dynasty' stands for the Antigonid kingdom from 306 (that dossier starts in 306); for 315-311 the counterpart is macedonian-empire, which holds Antigonus's Syria until its 306 split, and eu-02 is asked for the matching 315 gain of Syria and for a 246 gain of the Cyclades. (5) Left at confidence 1 (page silent): Greece occupation start/end are 308/304 (Ptolemy I and Demetrius pages; 303 is the end of Demetrius's range), Cilicia Aspera's loss in 30 (the Cilicia page gives 36 and 25 only). Cyprus: protectorate over the petty kings from 318, direct reconquest 313, lost 306, retaken 295, annexed by Rome 58, returned 47, Rome again 31; Ptolemy X as king of Cyprus 114-107 (a table entry on the Ptolemy VIII page) is not drawn. The Roman Cyprus page dates the Donations of Alexandria 'in 40 BC' against 34 on the Donations page; the Donations page was followed. (6) The 281-280 Cliopatria shape (95 k km2 over Macedon, Thessaly and Thrace) is Ptolemy Keraunos's Macedon, not Ptolemaic: keyframe wrong, ledger events deleted; Keraunos's Macedon needs a dossier. (7) Antony's eastern command in the Cliopatria shape of 31 is not Ptolemaic; the children's realms of the Donations (Armenia, Media, Parthia for Alexander Helios; Syria, Phoenicia and Cilicia for Ptolemy Philadelphus) are not drawn. (8) Rulers: identity.rulers follows the Ptolemaic dynasty page's list (principal ruler per period; co-rulers in the notes); Ptolemy VII has no dates and is omitted, and the page's own reign years for Ptolemy VIII (145-116 and 127-116) overlap. (9) The 126 shape drops 34 Egyptian cells (southern border) that no page explains. The 212 shape has a few cells at 7.1 E, an artefact. Pages disagree: Ptolemy I took Corinth in 308 (Ptolemy I page) or 309 (Ptolemaic page); Cyprus retaken 295 or 295/294; Ptolemy VIII was king of Cyrene and Cyprus 163-116 on the Apion page but only Cyrene on his own page.
